public.text: Interoperability is said to be represented as one capability in the architecture and realised through context-specific mechanisms. A single capability element may be too broad to support meaningful conformance, ownership, gap analysis, or implementation planning.
public.suggestedRevision: Decompose interoperability into subordinate capabilities such as service and endpoint discovery, identity and trust, transport, routing, orchestration, structural validation, semantic validation, mapping, consent enforcement, provenance, audit, and monitoring.
